title: Black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole): modeled ₹971/qtl left, Gadag → Bidar
summary: October 2022: reported black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole) prices at Gadag and Bidar imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 15 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹971 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 32 same-variety market pairs screened for black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole) in October 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Black Gram (Whole), FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Bidar report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: October 2022
scenes.caption: Gadag (Karnataka) and Bidar (Karnataka) both reported black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole) prices for the same variety and grade (Black Gram (Whole), FAQ) on 15 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Gadag reported a median ₹5,121 per quintal. Bidar reported a median ₹6,800 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,681/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,681 per quintal, and Bidar was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 418 km by road
scenes.caption: 418 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~6 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹90/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹1,002 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹650 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Bidar report, the rule selects 15 of 15 modeled shipping days. 15 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹971 per quintal (₹607 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole) route from Gadag to Bidar was positive on 100% of matched days in October 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹97,100, or ₹60,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹90/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Black Gram (Urd Beans, Whole) route from Gadag to Bidar was positive on 100% of matched days in October 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹97,100, or ₹60,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
